pairs.difference: A: the gold pan is tilted on a diagonal and spans almost the full width (0.86), with nuggets inside as the first read. B: the oil lamp stands upright, dead-centre and mirror-symmetric, with an even green sunburst all around. It is narrow (box width 0.426, below the real minimum of 0.558) and has the widest margins (0.115). This upright, centred, fully contained display matches the generated side of the lessons (front-on camera, centred lighthouse on its island).
pairs.fix: Draw the oil lamp larger and tilted about 15–20 degrees in a three-quarter view, so it fills more of the card width. Let the glass chimney come close to the top edge, and do not stand it perfectly centred and upright.

pairs.difference: A: the harmonica floats on a diagonal and is centred, with even pink space above and below. Its low box height (0.454) comes from the long, thin object. B: the fan is opened on a diagonal, pushed toward the upper right, and fills the card. Both use the same tilted, floating placement as the real telescope card, so composition gives no reason to pick one.

A: the cowboy hat is seen in three-quarter view, wide and low, with its brim nearly touching both side edges. B: the scout jacket is shown front-on, like a shop display. It is roughly symmetric with both sleeves spread out and sits centred on the green sunburst. The front-on, centred presentation leans toward the generated lessons.
pairs.fix: Show the jacket turned in three-quarter view, with one sleeve swinging toward the viewer, and draw it larger so the collar is close to the top edge. Do not lay it out flat and front-facing.

pairs.difference: A: the gas pump is angled slightly, standing on a slab with desert mesas on both sides, and the hose breaks the right side of its outline. B: the bell buoy is perfectly front-on and symmetric, with the bell centred in the hoop and the whole buoy sitting in the middle of the water with ripples on every side. Both margins are about 0.08, but B's mirror-symmetric, centred staging matches the generated lighthouse lessons.
pairs.fix: Turn the buoy to a three-quarter angle and move the camera closer, so the base is cut off by the bottom edge and the hoop nearly touches the top. Do not show the whole buoy floating dead-centre.

pairs.difference: A: the whole popcorn cart is shown on a tiled floor, from the awning down to the wheels, and is taller than any real card (box height 0.869). Every part sits inside the frame. B: the saddle on the hay bale is cropped by the right edge, with the bale running off the card, which is the same edge cropping the real fan and Ferris wheel cards use.
pairs.fix: Move in closer on the popcorn cart so the bottom of the wheels or one corner of the cart is cut off by the card edge. Make the awning and popcorn glass the main shape.

pairs.difference: A: the rocking chair is at a dynamic three-quarter angle and fills the card, with its rockers reaching toward the edges. B: the barrel stands perfectly front-on, upright and centred on a flat dirt floor. It is narrow (box width 0.544, below the real minimum of 0.661) and has more space around it than any real card (margin 0.119, above the real maximum of 0.098). This is the same centred, contained staging as the generated lessons.
pairs.fix: Draw the barrel bigger, turned in three-quarter view and slightly tilted, so it fills most of the card width and its top rim is close to the top edge.

pairs.difference: A: the pair of boots stands small in the middle with lots of empty purple space above and around. Its margin (0.121) is above the real maximum. B: the sneakers fill the full width and sit low, close to the side edges, against a wall and floor that split the card in half. A's floating small hero with wide empty margins is further from the real cards.
pairs.fix: Draw the boots larger, so the pair fills most of the card width and the tops of the shafts come near the top edge, leaving little empty background.

pairs.difference: A: the cactus is front-on and symmetric, with arms mirrored on either side and a flower centred on top, standing in the middle of a sand mound. B: the duck spring rider is in side view, facing left, with its beak pushing toward the left edge, so the shape is uneven and directional. The symmetric, centred cactus matches the generated lessons.
pairs.fix: Draw the cactus at a slight angle and off-centre, with one arm reaching closer to the viewer, and move the camera nearer so it fills more of the width.

pairs.difference: A: the three-tier fountain is centred and symmetric, and the whole basin fits inside the card on a paved floor. B: the covered wagon is at three-quarter view and cropped by the right edge, where the tongue runs off the card (margin 0.0), which is the same cropping the real cards use.
pairs.fix: Show the fountain from a three-quarter angle and closer in, so the front of the lower basin is cut off by the bottom edge and the tiers fill the card.

pairs.difference: B is the real lighthouse: a close-up whose tower is cut off by the bottom edge (margin 0.0), with the lantern room as the first read. A: the windmill is small and shown whole on a stone base, with lots of sky and grass around it (subject area 0.211, below the real range; margin 0.121, above it). This is the generated habit of showing the complete object staged on a ground plane.
pairs.fix: Zoom in on the windmill so the wheel and tower top fill the card and the tower legs are cut off by the bottom edge. Do not show the base and surrounding ground.

pairs.difference: A: the campfire shares the card with a lit cabin window at the top left, a crescent moon, and a large kettle on a rock at the right, so several bright spots compete with the hero. B: the binocular viewer is a single close-up hero, with its pole cropped by the bottom edge like the real fan card, against a soft city background.
pairs.fix: Make the campfire the only hero. Remove the cabin, moon and kettle, move the camera closer so the ring of logs and stones fills the card, and keep the background dark and simple.

pairs.difference: A: the neck pillow is a large, roughly front-on shape centred in the card, with the most occupancy of any card (0.418, at the top of the real range). B: the water bottle floats tilted on a diagonal across the sunburst, like the real telescope card. A's front-on, centred mass leans generated.
pairs.fix: Tilt the neck pillow into a three-quarter view and shift it slightly off-centre, so it reads as an object turned in space rather than a flat front-on shape.

pattern: Generated cards stage the object front-on, mirror-symmetric and dead-centre, shown complete on a little base, island or floor with even space around it, and sometimes add side props that compete with it. Real cards use a turned or tilted three-quarter view, move in closer, and let the edge of the card cut off the object (the lighthouse base, the fan pole, the wagon tongue).
